notes: Consumed by sdk, sdk-python and audit-verifier per .claude/tickets/PA01-CONTRACT-action-fixtures.md. `canonicalUtf8` is byte-for-byte (as a UTF-8 string); `sha256Hex` is jcsCommitment(value). Cases with `expectThrow: true` have no canonical/hash — the implementation MUST refuse them; `throwReasonContains` is a substring every conforming implementation's error message should be checkable against (not required to match verbatim across languages, only in spirit).

cases.name: key-ordering-flat
cases.description: Object keys re-emitted in UTF-16-code-unit sorted order regardless of insertion order.

cases.name: key-ordering-nested
cases.description: Sorting is recursive at every object depth.

cases.name: unicode-basic
cases.description: Non-ASCII characters are emitted raw (UTF-8), not \u-escaped, matching RFC 8785 string serialization.

cases.name: non-bmp-key-sort-order
cases.description: RFC 8785 mandates UTF-16 CODE-UNIT sort order, not code-point order. A key starting with a surrogate pair (U+10437, code units D801 DC37) sorts BEFORE a BMP key U+FFFF, because 0xD801 < 0xFFFF as code UNITS — even though U+10437 > U+FFFF as a code POINT. An implementation that sorts by code point (a common bug) gets this backwards.

cases.name: proto-literal-key
cases.description: TICKET-213 precedent: a JSON object with a literal "__proto__" key (as produced by JSON.parse, an own enumerable data property) must canonicalize as an ordinary key, never resolve through the prototype chain or vanish.

cases.name: constructor-and-toString-literal-keys
cases.description: Same trap class as __proto__ — 'constructor' and 'toString' are inherited Object.prototype members that must still canonicalize as ordinary own keys when present in the parsed JSON.

cases.name: control-char-escaping
cases.description: Control characters below U+0020 use the shorthand escapes where defined (\t \n) and \u00XX otherwise; the double-quote and backslash are always escaped.

cases.name: number-negative-zero
cases.description: RFC 8785 §3.2.2.3: signed zero MUST serialize as "0", matching ECMAScript Number::toString(-0). NOTE: JSON does not have a syntax that keeps -0 distinguishable from 0 once round-tripped through a JS object and re-serialized by a generic JSON.stringify (which is how this fixture file itself was generated) — a consuming implementation should additionally unit-test its own in-memory -0 handling directly (see jcs-canonical.spec.ts) rather than relying on this fixture file's on-disk text to carry the sign bit.

cases.name: number-large-exponent
cases.description: 1e21 is the ECMAScript threshold where Number::toString switches to exponential notation.

cases.name: number-above-max-safe-integer
cases.description: 9007199254740993 has no exact IEEE-754 double representation and rounds to 9007199254740992 at JSON.parse time, BEFORE this module ever sees it — both TS and Python float64 parsers must agree on this rounding for the fixture to byte-compare.

cases.name: duplicate-key-in-source-text
cases.description: A JSON TEXT with a duplicate key (`{"a":1,"a":2}`) is only representable via JSON.parse (a JS object literal cannot have the duplicate) — parse collapses to the LAST value per the JSON spec, so there is nothing left for this module to deduplicate. Included to document the behavior, not to test this module's own logic.

cases.name: absent-vs-explicit-null
cases.description: An omitted key and an explicit null key are semantically and byte-wise distinct.

cases.name: lone-high-surrogate
cases.description: A string containing an unpaired UTF-16 high surrogate cannot be encoded to well-formed UTF-8 without a lossy substitution (U+FFFD) that TS and Python encoders are documented to diverge on (SEC-PA01-11(b)). This implementation REFUSES rather than risk a cross-language byte mismatch on an attacker-reachable path.

cases.name: non-finite-number-nan
cases.note: Represented as a sentinel string in this JSON fixture file (NaN is not valid JSON); the consuming test substitutes the real NaN value before calling the implementation.

cases.name: mcp-action-envelope-example
cases.description: The exact shape D2 defines for the managed-MCP canonical request. The COMMITMENT excludes the `version` discriminant (only protocol/target/tool/arguments are hashed) — see computeMcpActionRequestCommitment.
